mentions.text:
Some updates on bottleneck timelines: 

- ABF substrates: 1 year 
/ eg. Ajinomoto (2802) for ABF film, Ibiden, Unimicron, Nan Ya PCB, etc make the substrates 

- HDI Boards: Over 6 months 
/ Victory Giant (300476), Zhen Ding (4958), Unimicron, Compeq (2313), Meiko (6787)

- Multilayer boards: ~6 months 
/ Victory Giant, WUS (002463), $TTMI, Gold Circuit Electronics (2368), 

- CCL: Over 6 months (severe shortages of materials) 
/ Elite Material (2383), Shengyi (600183), TUC (6274), ITEQ (6213), Nan Ya Plastics (1303), Resonac (4004)
Mitsui Kinzoku (5706) / HVLP copper foil.  Nittobo / glass fiber/cloth

- MLCCs, chip resistors, tantalum capacitors, aluminum electrolytic capacitors: 15-20 weeks to 1 year+

MLCC: Murata (6981), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, TDK (6762), Taiyo Yuden (6976), Yageo (2327), Walsin (2492)
Chip Resistors: Yageo, Walsin, KOA (6999), Rohm (6963) and $VSH
Tantalum capacitors: Kyocera/AVX, Yageo/KEMET, $VSH again

Aluminum electrolytic capacitors: Nippon Chemi-Con (6997) Nichicon (6996) | Timelines sourced from Digitimes, did the honors of adding in related companies. 

But it's slightly more nuanced since MLCCs and others mix. in commodity types vs. AI DCs.

Regardless, just some helpful mapping.

reasons: gets paid between the grid and the chip
mentions.text:
Per Truist, AI data center capacity goes from 24 GW to 100 GW by 2030, and every one of those watts has to be converted, stored, smoothed and cooled before a single GPU turns on.

So I mapped every business that gets paid between the grid and the chip, seven layers from the grid to the GPU, and marked the one I'd watch most closely.

Infrastructure // getting megawatts into the building:
$ETN Eaton, $VRT Vertiv, $GEV GE Vernova, $SBGSY Schneider, $ABBNY ABB

Power supply // AC in, DC out:
Delta (https://t.co/tAcP8vyGJW), the cleanest pure play on the whole map Lite-On (https://t.co/RZNOwxTpNN), co-designed the GB300 power shelf $FLEX Flex, $AEIS Advanced Energy

DC-DC conversion // the last step before the silicon, and THE LAYER I'D WATCH:
$MPWR Monolithic Power, $VICR Vicor, $IFNNY Infineon, $TXN Texas Instruments, $ADI Analog Devices, $RNECY Renesas, $ON onsemi
As density rises, every point of efficiency here is worth more, and that's where pricing power can show up.

Battery backup // seconds to minutes when power drops:
$PCRFY Panasonic, Samsung SDI (006400.KS), LG Energy Solution (373220.KS) 

Capacitors // fractions of a second when GPU demand spikes:
Nippon Chemi-Con (6997.T), $MRAAY Murata, $TTDKY TDK, Yageo (https://t.co/yXXDTFGgaV), Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150.KS)

Control // the nervous system:
$NXPI NXP, $STM STMicro, plus TI, ADI and Infineon again

Cooling // where every watt ends up:
$VRT Vertiv, Delta, $NJDCY Nidec

Panasonic shows up in six boxes on the map and Delta in four, and to me that's the tell, because the names that keep popping up are the ones getting paid more than once every time a rack gets built.

I broke down all seven layers in my latest article on Substack, including why they grow on three different demand curves and the five holes in the thesis, because I don't do one-sided. 

It's free to read, link in the comments.
